argument_summary: The cleanest supportable position from the admissible record is narrower than the original claim: this was a risk-based rejection because the vendor had not cleared approval at the time of decision, not because the file proved a reject-level control failure on any single item. BPROC-022-C and BPROC-022-D show unresolved quality/control diligence concerns, BPROC-022-E shows procurement itself documented that follow-up was required before approval if storage controls remained unresolved, and BPROC-022-B adds a non-clean prior delivery signal. That combination supports a bounded conclusion that approval conditions were unmet when the decision was taken. The packet should therefore be treated as at most caveated support for rejection, rather than a definitive showing of a material control failure.
claims_about_policy: Policy does not permit treating the quality-process gap or questionnaire inconsistency, standing alone, as proof of a reject-level control failure. The defensible policy reading is instead that a vendor may be denied approval where admissible diligence remains unresolved at decision time and the file shows approval was contingent on follow-up that had not been completed. On that narrower reading, the decision can be defended only as a caveated failure to satisfy approval threshold, not as clean proof that policy required rejection.
claims_about_business_cost: Reopening the vendor decision would impose avoidable procurement delay, and the admissible record is sufficient to avoid that step if the audit treatment is narrowed. A caveated compliance finding is lower cost and better matched to the evidence than escalation, because the remaining weakness is overstatement of policy certainty rather than absence of any admissible risk basis.
concessions: The current record does not cleanly demonstrate a documented materiality determination rising to reject-level control failure.
The statement that price advantage did not outweigh risk is not independently supported by an admissible balancing method in the file.
BPROC-022-E supports follow-up before approval more directly than it supports outright rejection.
The strongest defensible claim is failure to clear approval conditions, not proven control failure.
private_or_side_channel_content: No new evidence is offered. No private or side-channel material is relied on or cited.
